title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S is a base ring with divided powers (p.d.), and 𝒜_1 = S{X_0, dX_0} is the free divided-power de Rham algebra in one variable. This is the p.d. de Rham complex of a 1-simplex (an 'interval'). It can be presented as S{X_0,X_1,dX_0,dX_1}/(X_0+X_1−T, dX_0+dX_1)_{p.d.}. α: 𝒜_1 → S is an augmentation with Ker α = 𝒜^+.

(1) Classification of endomorphisms. Endomorphisms φ of 𝒜_1 as an augmented differential graded S-algebra correspond exactly to the image ξ_1 = φ(X_0) ∈ Ker α. Write ξ_1 = A_1 + B_1 dX_0 with A_1 ∈ S{X_0}^+ (augmentation ideal) and B_1 ∈ S{X_0} arbitrary. φ(dX_0) is then dξ_1.

(2) Corollary: if φ respects the grading, the differential and the augmented algebra structure, it automatically respects divided powers. Reason: d(φ(X^{(i)})) = φ(X^{(i-1)})·dφ(X), and d(φ(X)^{(i)}) = φ(X)^{(i-1)} dφ(X). By induction on i the two elements φ(X^{(i)}) and φ(X)^{(i)} have the same differential. By the p.d. Poincaré lemma their difference is a constant in S. Both lie in Ker α, so the constant is 0. Note that (A+B dX)^{(i)} = A^{(i)} + A^{(i-1)}B dX makes sense because A lies in the p.d. ideal and (B dX)^2 = 0.

(3) Specialisation. Take S = k{T} with p.d. ideal k{T}^+, so that α (X_0↦0, X_1↦T) is compatible with all structures, p.d. included. Define a second augmentation β: 𝒜_1 → S by X_0↦T, X_1↦0, dX_0↦0, which is compatible because the differential on S is trivial. These are the two endpoint evaluations of the 'path object'. One studies φ compatible with both α and β. The condition βφ = β amounts to β(φ(X_0^{(i)})) = T^{(i)} for all i ≥ 1. Since φ(X_0^{(i)}) = A_1^{(i)} + B_i dX_0, this becomes β(A_1)^{(i)} = T^{(i)}, i.e. β(A_1) = T (for i = 1, and then all i follow).

Purpose: this is a step toward understanding the automorphisms/homotopies of the divided-power de Rham complex of simplices, i.e. a p.d. (integral / char p) analogue of Sullivan's polynomial forms ∇(p,•), presumably for the 1976 IHÉS lecture on an integral homotopy-theoretic de Rham theory.
errors: Minor notational slip: 'β(A_1)^{(i)} = T^{(i)}' should be read as β(A_1^{(i)}) = β(A_1)^{(i)} = T^{(i)}. The condition reduces to β(A_1) = T, since β respects p.d.

The Corollary's proof is not written on the page. It relies on the p.d. Poincaré lemma (closed degree-0 elements of S{X} are constants) plus the augmentation, which hold; no error, only an unstated step.
The condition is written as βφ = β (with a variant symbol); this is consistent.

ideas.what: Free divided-power de Rham algebra S{X, dX} of the 1-simplex, presented as S{X_0,X_1,dX_0,dX_1}/(X_0+X_1−T, dX_0+dX_1), with endpoint augmentations α, β
ideas.modern_name: divided-power (integral) analogue of Sullivan's simplicial polynomial de Rham forms / path object
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (rational, 1977); integral or divided-power variants by Cenkl–Porter and later authors (unsure of exact attribution)
ideas.where_published: 1976 IHÉS lecture not published as far as I know

ideas.what: Endomorphisms of the augmented free p.d. dga in one variable are classified by ξ = A + B dX with A in the augmentation ideal
ideas.modern_name: universal property of free p.d. dg-algebras

ideas.what: A dg-augmented-algebra endomorphism of S{X,dX} automatically preserves divided powers
ideas.modern_name: rigidity of p.d. structure via p.d. Poincaré lemma

missed.claim: Grothendieck is building the p.d. de Rham complex of simplices with endpoint augmentations as a path object, i.e. an integral/char-p analogue of Sullivan's rational models. Here p.d. structure is forced by dga structure. This anticipates later work on integral or p-adic de Rham models of homotopy types (divided-power cochain models, Mandell's E∞ p-adic models, derived de Rham).
missed.quote: Si φ respecte la gr. diff. et la structure d'algèbre différentielle augmentée alors φ respecte les p.d. !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical evidence of an unpublished 1975–76 Grothendieck program on divided-power de Rham models for homotopy. It is of mild interest for the history of integral rational-homotopy-type theory. The individual computations are routine.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains elementary computations (endomorphisms of the free p.d. dga on one generator, automatic p.d.-compatibility). Its interest is mainly as a witness of an unpublished program on p.d. de Rham models of simplices, not a new result.
